symptom.duration: Patient noticed a painless lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast approximately 2 months ago. examination_results.Physical Examination: Left breast inspection reveals a 3.5 x 2.7 cm firm, immobile mass located in the upper outer quadrant, 2 cm from the areolar margin. Overlying skin displays focal erythema and pronounced dimpling measuring 1.2 cm in diameter. There is noted skin thickening and loss of normal contour. Palpation elicits mild tenderness with no warmth. Left nipple displays a faint serous, non-bloody discharge on expression. Axillary assessment detects two enlarged, non-tender lymph nodes in the left axilla, each approximately 1.5 cm in diameter, with firm consistency and limited mobility. No supraclavicular lymphadenopathy observed. Right breast and contralateral axilla unremarkable. No visible edema or satellite skin nodules.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Mammography of the left breast demonstrates a dense, irregular mass measuring approximately 3.4 x 2.6 cm with spiculated borders in the upper outer quadrant. Associated segmental architectural distortion and subtle microcalcifications are present within and adjacent to the lesion. Ultrasound reveals a hypoechoic, irregular mass with indistinct margins and posterior acoustic shadowing, measuring 3.3 x 2.5 x 2.0 cm; Doppler imaging shows moderate internal vascularity. Two oval hypoechoic axillary lymph nodes identified (largest: 1.5 x 0.8 cm) with cortical thickening greater than 3 mm. Contrast-enhanced breast MRI confirms a 3.6 x 2.8 x 2.2 cm mass exhibiting rapid initial enhancement (wash-in rate: 110%) and early washout kinetics. No multicentric or contralateral disease seen. No evidence of chest wall invasion.
examination_results.Tissue Biopsy: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy yields 4 core samples from the left breast mass. Histopathology reveals invasive epithelial proliferation forming irregular nests with prominent nuclear atypia, increased mitotic activity (25 mitoses per 10 high-power fields), and moderate stromal desmoplasia. Tumor extends to within 0.2 mm of inked margin in one core. Multiple foci of lymphovascular invasion identified. Axillary lymph node core biopsy demonstrates partial effacement by atypical cells consistent with epithelial origin.
examination_results.Breast Cancer Tumor Marker Examination: Serum tumor marker results: CA15-3: 46 U/mL (normal <25 U/mL); CEA: 7.0 ng/mL (normal <5.0 ng/mL); CA125: 22 U/mL (normal <35 U/mL). All other relevant markers within reference range. No evidence of tumor marker elevation suggestive of widespread systemic involvement.
examination_results.Immunohistochemical Examination: Immunohistochemical staining of core biopsy: Estrogen Receptor (ER): positive (85% of nuclei); Progesterone Receptor (PR): positive (65% of nuclei); HER-2/neu: negative (0, IHC score 1+); Ki-67 proliferation index: 28%. E-cadherin positive, confirming epithelial origin. p53: focal (20%) positivity. No basal cytokeratin overexpression.

examination_results.Imaging Tests: Mammography (bilateral): Left breast shows a dense, irregular mass measuring 6.2 x 6.0 cm with spiculated margins in the upper outer quadrant; extensive architectural distortion; significant overlying skin thickening (4.8 mm vs contralateral 1.9 mm); nipple inversion; multiple enlarged, irregular axillary lymph nodes with loss of fatty hilum; cluster of microcalcifications in adjacent parenchyma. Right breast: scattered fibroglandular density, no suspicious lesion. Breast ultrasound: Left side mass hypoechoic, 6.4 x 5.8 x 4.2 cm, marked posterior shadowing; several satellite nodular lesions (up to 1.2 cm); prominent skin edema. Doppler shows increased central and peripheral vascularity. Axillary region: conglomerate lymph nodes (largest 2.8 x 2.5 cm), loss of ovality, hypoechoic cortex >4 mm. Left upper limb: mild subcutaneous edema. Breast MRI: Large irregular enhancing mass infiltrating overlying skin and pectoral fascia (skin invasion evident), multiple small rim-enhancing cutaneous nodules; evidence of multicentric satellite lesions within 2–3 cm of primary mass; thickened dermis, edema of subcutaneous fat. examination_results.Tissue Biopsy: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the left breast mass yielded multiple gray-white tissue cores (up to 2.5 cm). Histopathologic analysis shows densely packed sheets of pleomorphic epithelial cells with marked nuclear atypia, high mitotic activity (>18 mitoses/10 HPF), frequent abnormal mitoses, and conspicuous nucleoli. Tumor infiltration into adjacent adipose and fibrous tissue observed. Lymphovascular invasion and invasive growth pattern present. Background shows marked desmoplastic reaction. Cobblestone-like arrangement of tumor cells with areas of necrosis. Skin nodule biopsy also reveals tumor cell invasion into subdermal tissue. Axillary node aspirate contains metastatic epithelial cells with nuclear pleomorphism and mitosis. No evidence of in situ pathology isolated in this sample.

examination_results.Immunohistochemical Examination: Immunostaining of tumor tissue reveals estrogen receptor (ER): negative (<1% nuclei positive), progesterone receptor (PR): negative (<1% nuclei positive), HER-2/neu: strongly positive (3+ by IHC, uniform intense membrane staining in >30% of tumor cells), Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirms gene amplification. Ki-67 proliferation index: 70% (markedly elevated, indicating high cell turnover/aggressiveness). E-cadherin positive, p53 diffusely positive, EGFR positive. Tumor cells negative for GCDFP-15 and low molecular weight cytokeratin. Lymphovascular invasion highlighted by D2-40. Findings indicative of highly proliferative, hormone receptor-negative, HER2-positive tumor biology.

examination_results.Tissue Biopsy: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the breast mass: Microscopy displays invasive growth of pleomorphic epithelial cells, forming solid nests and cords, marked nuclear atypia, numerous mitotic figures (>25/10 HPF), and areas of necrosis. examination_results.Breast Cancer Tumor Marker Examination: Serum CA15-3: 79.2 U/mL (reference: 0–30); Serum CEA: 17.6 ng/mL (reference: 0–5); Serum CA125: 52.7 U/mL (reference: 0–35). All markers above normal limits, consistent with extensive disease burden.

Pain and heaviness intensify by the end of the day and improve after lying down or reducing the lump. Occasional mild abdominal discomfort and constipation have developed in the last few weeks.

examination_results.Imaging Tests: Groin ultrasound reveals a defect in the left inguinal canal measuring approximately 2.1 cm in diameter, with herniation of hyperechoic omental fat and small loops of bowel seen protruding through the defect. The herniated contents are reducible upon gentle probe pressure, and peristalsis is observed within the hernial sac, confirming bowel involvement. No evidence of bowel wall thickening, reduced perfusion, or incarcerated contents. Mild subcutaneous edema adjacent to the defect is present. No fluid collection or abscess formation. Both testes and spermatic cord structures appear normal. Abdominal CT (optional for moderate cases): Axial and coronal images demonstrate protrusion of preperitoneal fat and a short segment of small intestine (measuring approximately 2.9 cm) through the left inguinal canal. The bowel wall enhances normally and there is no sign of obstruction, ischemia, or free intraperitoneal air. No significant lymphadenopathy or other intra-abdominal abnormalities.

lifestyle_factor: heavy alcohol use (frequent beer and spirits consumption)

symptom.duration: Symptoms began approximately 2 months ago with intermittent discomfort. Over the past 3 weeks, the mass has enlarged and become more noticeable, with moderate pain and heaviness especially after prolonged standing or exertion.

examination_results.Imaging Tests: Ultrasound of the right inguinal region reveals a 3.5 cm x 2.0 cm hypoechoic protrusion traversing the inguinal canal with clear continuity from intra-abdominal tissue. The mass demonstrates peristaltic movement on dynamic exam and increases in size with Valsalva maneuver, measuring up to 4.2 cm x 2.5 cm during strain. Contents appear to be intestinal loops with preserved wall vascularity on color Doppler imaging; no signs of bowel wall edema or fluid collection are noted. The lesion is compressible and reducible with gentle probe pressure; no evidence of ulceration or soft-tissue masses. Surrounding soft tissue echo appears normal without localized lymphadenopathy. On the unaffected left side, no abnormal mass or defect is observed. Abdominal wall thickness and muscle architecture are otherwise within age-appropriate limits. No free fluid or abnormal intra-abdominal findings detected.

Symptoms remain moderate without rapid progression.

examination_results.Breast Ultrasound: Left breast: At the 2 o'clock position, 2.1 cm from the areola, a hypoechoic, irregularly contoured area measuring 1.6 x 0.9 cm is visualized. Lesion is poorly circumscribed, with mixed internal echoes and no obvious posterior acoustic shadowing. Surrounding parenchyma shows localized thickening and multiple small, uniform echoic nodules (maximum diameter 0.3 cm). Ductal structures are slightly dilated (2.8 mm) in the periareolar region with some fluid content, but no solid mass seen within ducts. Axillary lymph nodes are normal in size and morphology. No evidence of abnormal vascularity on color Doppler. Right breast: Glandular tissue homogeneous, no focal lesions detected.
examination_results.Breast Mammography: Craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views reveal an ill-defined area of glandular density in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, measuring approximately 1.7 x 1.0 cm. There is no evidence of spiculated mass or suspicious microcalcifications. Adjacent glandular tissues appear moderately dense, with no skin retraction or architectural distortion. No abnormal findings in the right breast. Axillary regions are unremarkable.
examination_results.Ductal Endoscope, Ductal Angiography: Ductal endoscopy of the left breast reveals segmental ductal ectasia in one major duct with mild erythematous changes of the ductal epithelium. No intraductal papillary lesions, necrosis, or hemorrhagic material visualized. Ductal angiography demonstrates a single, tortuous duct measuring 2.9 mm in diameter with smooth, regular walls, and contrast media flows unimpeded—no filling defects detected. Samples of ductal discharge cytology showed abundant ductal epithelial cells, scattered foam cells, and rare lymphocytes; atypical cells were not observed.
examination_results.Pathological Examination: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the palpable nodule obtained. Histopathology shows an increased number of ductal and lobular epithelial cells with focal sclerosing adenosis and proliferation of small glandular acini. Stromal fibrosis and local glandular thickening are present, with mild periductal lymphocytic infiltration. Cellular atypia is absent. No evidence of significant mitoses, necrosis, or malignant transformation.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Breast MRI (T2-weighted imaging): Localized glandular thickening and segmental non-mass enhancement in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, corresponding to the area of maximal pain and palpable nodule. Enhancement pattern is homogeneous; kinetic curve demonstrates persistent type I (benign) pattern. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion, or abnormal enhancement elsewhere. Overlying skin and chest wall structures appear intact.

symptom.duration: Symptoms began three months ago with mild pain and slowly progressed to severe, disabling pain and tenderness over the past month. Multiple hypoechoic nodules are observed throughout both breasts, ranging from 7 mm to 22 mm in diameter. The left breast contains a dominant irregular hypoechoic mass measuring 21 x 17 mm with poorly defined margins. Multiple smaller cystic lesions are interspersed among areas of solid nodules. Doppler imaging shows moderate internal vascularity within the larger mass and increased peri-lesional flow. No axillary lymphadenopathy detected.
examination_results.Breast Mammography: Mammographic imaging demonstrates dense glandular patterns bilaterally with extensive areas of glandular thickening. Multiple round and irregular opacities are noted in both breasts, the largest in the left breast, measuring 2.2 cm. Several regions of segmental microcalcifications are apparent, predominantly in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast (approximate area 6 cm²). No definitive architectural distortion is seen; skin and nipple thickening are noted on the left side. No evident signs of invasive features are present.
examination_results.Ductal Endoscope, Ductal Angiography: Ductal endoscopy of the left breast reveals dilated ducts containing friable, erythematous mucosa. A focal intraductal lesion measuring 8 mm is visualized with evidence of recent bleeding in the central duct system. Multiple smaller nodular areas are noted along the ductal walls. Ductal angiography shows irregular filling defects and partial ductal obstruction in the left retroareolar region. Cytological sampling from within the duct yields numerous epithelial cells with mild atypia and abundant red blood cells; no malignant cells identified.
examination_results.Pathological Examination: Core needle biopsy is performed on the largest left breast nodule and peri-nipple area. Microscopic examination reveals excessive ductal and lobular epithelial proliferation with florid papillary structures and sclerosing adenosis. Stromal fibrosis and periductal edema are evident. Occasional focal areas of epithelial atypia are present; no evidence of invasive cellular features. Extensive intraductal hemorrhage is confirmed. Immunohistochemical staining shows strong ER positivity in the affected regions; Ki-67 proliferation index moderately elevated at 18%.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Contrast-enhanced MRI of the breasts reveals diffuse, asymmetric glandular enhancement, more pronounced in the left breast. Multifocal nodular lesions with moderate contrast uptake are seen throughout both breasts, largest lesion measures 2.2 x 1.7 cm in the left upper outer quadrant. Additional linear and segmental enhancement in the retroareolar region corresponds with ductal thickening and partial obstruction. No evidence of extramammary extension or axillary nodal enlargement.
